title: Gentiles Seeking God vs. Israel Conquering Edom
summary: St. James at the Council of Jerusalem settles the circumcision controversy by quoting Amos 9 from the Septuagint. The Hebrew Masoretic Text predicts a military conquest of Edom, making James's argument impossible on the Protestant Hebrew text.

doll1_reading.label: Doll 1: Master English Text (Acts 15:16–17)
doll1_reading.text: ‘After this I will return, and I will rebuild the tent of David that has fallen; I will rebuild its ruins, and I will restore it, that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by my name, says the Lord, who makes these things known from of old.’

doll2_rationale.label: Doll 2: Translation Rationale & Syntax Breakdown
doll2_rationale.content: The Greek clause uses the conjunction ὅπως ἄν (hopōs an) with the subjunctive ἐκζητήσωσιν (ekzētēsōsin, 'that they may seek diligently'), followed by the accusative τὸν Κύριον ('the Lord'). The grammatical subject is οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων ('the remnant of mankind'). The New Testament author faithfully reproduces the Septuagint's universal salvation theology rather than conforming the text to the nationalistic Hebrew Masoretic reading.

title: A Body Prepared vs. Ears Dug / Pierced
summary: Hebrews 10 argues that the Levitical animal sacrifices are abolished by Christ's Incarnate Body ('a body you prepared for me'). In the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the word 'body' does not exist; it reads 'ears you have dug for me.'

doll1_reading.label: Doll 1: Master English Text (Hebrews 10:5–7)
doll1_reading.text: Consequently, when Christ came into the world, he said, ‘Sacrifices and offerings you have not desired, but a body you have prepared for me; in burnt offerings and sin offerings you have taken no pleasure. Then I said, Behold, I have come to do your will, O God, as it is written of me in the scroll of the book.’

doll2_rationale.label: Doll 2: Translation Rationale & Syntax Breakdown
doll2_rationale.content: The author of Hebrews bases his entire theological argument in verse 10 ('sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all') upon the word σῶμα (sōma, 'body'). In verse 8–9, the author argues: 'He abolishes the first in order to establish the second.' If the Old Testament said only 'ears,' the physical offering of Christ's incarnate flesh as the replacement of animal sacrifice lacks its biblical prooftext.

doll1_reading.text: Now Nahash, king of the Ammonites, severely oppressed the Gadites and the Reubenites, and he gouged out the right eye of all of them, and brought terror and fear on Israel. There was not a man left among the Israelites beyond the Jordan whose right eye was not gouged out by Nahash king of the Ammonites, except that seven thousand men had fled from the Ammonites and entered Jabesh-gilead. And about a month later, Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead...
